prompt: KnightMotives' outdated ERP, which stays on-premises for now, holds dealer promotions and discounts. Leadership wants to expose a promotions API to about 400 dealers' existing sales tools and to third-party tool vendors without modifying the ERP. The ERP can sustain only a few dozen requests per second and cannot issue or revoke credentials. Dealers have no budget for new equipment, so their tools will call over the internet. The business needs self-service onboarding, a different monthly call allowance for each partner tier, and protection of the ERP from bursts. Which design fits?

choices.text: Publish the API through Apigee proxies that reach the ERP over the hybrid link, with API products, per-tier quotas, spike arrest and a developer portal
choices.rationale: Apigee's proxy layer fronts an unchanged backend and supplies credentials, Quota policies that can differ by API product, app or developer, and SpikeArrest against sudden bursts. Quota enforces partner contracts while SpikeArrest protects the backend, and a portal covers onboarding.

choices.text: Expose the ERP through an external Application Load Balancer with a hybrid network endpoint group and Cloud Armor rate limiting keyed on a partner header
choices.rationale: This throttles requests per key and keeps the ERP off the internet, but it has no notion of API products, contractual call allowances per tier, credential issuance or a developer onboarding portal, so the team would build them.

choices.text: Wrap the ERP in a Cloud Run service that caps its maximum instances and concurrency, and have each dealer tool call that service with IAM authentication
choices.rationale: Capping instances and concurrency limits load, but not per partner, and IAM invoker authentication needs Google identities that third-party dealer tools do not have. It also provides no allowances per tier and no onboarding.

choices.text: Replicate the promotion tables into BigQuery on a schedule and grant each dealer tool read access to them through per-dealer IAM roles
choices.rationale: A copy would shield the ERP, but promotions would be stale between loads, existing dealer tools would need Google identities and BigQuery integration, and there would still be no per-tier allowances or onboarding portal.

explanation: An API management layer lets legacy backends stay unchanged while adding credentials, tiered quotas, burst protection and onboarding.

prompt: Brightwave Genomics keeps hundreds of terabytes of sequencing archives on an on-premises NAS and must land them in Cloud Storage this quarter. The site shares a modest internet uplink with clinical staff, and the network team estimates that uploading over it would take many months. Security requires the data to be protected with an encryption key the company controls in Cloud KMS. Which approach fits best?

choices.text: Install Storage Transfer Service agents next to the NAS and let the scheduled job run over the existing internet uplink until it finishes
choices.rationale: Storage Transfer Service is a good online tool for on-premises data, but it still moves bytes over the same shared uplink. The stem says that path takes many months, so the deadline is missed.

choices.text: Order a Transfer Appliance, copy the archives onto it locally, ship it back, and let Google load the data into your bucket
choices.rationale: Correct. Transfer Appliance is the offline option when a network upload would take more than about a week. Data is encrypted on the device, customer-managed Cloud KMS keys are supported, and Google uploads the data into your Cloud Storage bucket.

choices.text: Order a Dedicated Interconnect circuit and run parallel gcloud storage copy jobs once the new link has been provisioned and tested
choices.rationale: A faster link can move data, but provisioning a circuit is its own lead-time project and a recurring cost, which is out of proportion for a one-time bulk move. It is the common reflex of fixing bandwidth instead of switching to an offline transfer.

choices.text: Replicate the NAS with Migrate to Virtual Machines, which copies disks continuously and can then place the files in Cloud Storage
choices.rationale: Migrate to Virtual Machines replicates VM disks into Compute Engine for lift-and-shift cut-over. It is not a bulk file-transfer tool and does not write file archives into a bucket.

explanation: Choose the transfer tool by the arithmetic of data volume against available bandwidth: when an online upload would take more than about a week, an offline Transfer Appliance shipment is the designed path.

prompt: A compliance script at Cymbal Audit counts the objects in a Cloud Storage bucket by calling the JSON API list method directly over HTTP. The team knows the bucket holds far more objects than the script reports, and no errors or retries appear in the logs. The exhibit shows what the script receives and prints. What should you recommend?

choices.text: Raise the maxResults value in the request so that the whole bucket is returned in a single response and no token is issued
choices.rationale: maxResults only sets the size of each page. Listing a large bucket still comes back in pages, and the returned token is the signal that more results remain, so a bigger page does not replace the loop.

choices.text: Request a higher read quota for the project, since the service is silently truncating results once the quota has been reached
choices.rationale: Hitting a quota produces explicit errors such as a 429 response, not a successful 200 with partial data. Truncation here is normal pagination, so quota is the wrong diagnosis.

choices.text: Resend the request with pageToken set to the returned nextPageToken until none comes back, or use a client library iterator
choices.rationale: Correct. A nextPageToken in the response means the listing is incomplete. The script must keep requesting pages until the token is absent. Client libraries paginate by default and return an iterator that does this.

choices.text: Wrap the list call in exponential backoff and retry it until the full set arrives, because the partial reply is a transient server fault
choices.rationale: Backoff is the right tool for transient errors. A 200 response with a token is a complete, healthy reply to that page. Retrying the same request just returns the same first page again.

explanation: Distinguish errors from pagination: success status with a next-page token means the caller must fetch more pages, whereas quota and transient faults show up as error codes.

prompt: Altitude Freight runs two VMware VMs it wants off its data center. One hosts a Tomcat web tier that the platform team wants running on GKE without any code rewrite. The other runs a licensed analytics package that is tied to a hardware ID and depends on a kernel-mode NFS driver, and it must keep working unchanged. What migration plan should you advise?

choices.text: Run the fit assessment on both VMs, containerize the Tomcat tier with Migrate to Containers, and rehost the analytics VM with Migrate to Virtual Machines
choices.rationale: Correct. Tomcat middleware is a good fit for Migrate to Containers. Kernel drivers and hardware-tied licenses are listed as poor fits for containers, so that VM is better lifted to Compute Engine with Migrate to Virtual Machines.

choices.text: Containerize both VMs with Migrate to Containers, because it accepts VMware sources, and fix any failures that appear during GKE testing
choices.rationale: Supported sources do not mean every workload is a fit. Special kernel drivers and hardware-ID licensing are called out as poor fits, so skipping the assessment just moves the failure to test time.

choices.text: Rehost both VMs on Compute Engine with Migrate to Virtual Machines now, and leave any containerization for a later refactoring project
choices.rationale: This is safe for the analytics VM but ignores the stated goal for the web tier. A purpose-built tool already containerizes a good-fit Tomcat tier without a rewrite, so deferring it is unnecessary.

choices.text: Rewrite both applications as microservices before moving anything, since only code written natively for containers can run on GKE
choices.rationale: This is the myth that containers need a rewrite. Migrate to Containers modernizes existing VM workloads into containers without changing application code, so a rewrite first adds cost and delay.

explanation: Assess each VM's container fit first. Good-fit middleware goes to containers on GKE, and workloads that depend on kernel drivers or hardware-bound licenses are rehosted as VMs.
